questions.text:
Consider a simple random walk model constructed as a sum of independent and identically distributed random variables, \[ S_T = \sum_{t=1}^T z_t \] where the increments \(z_t\) are standard random variables satisfying \(\mathbb{E}[z_t]=0\) and \(\mathbb{E}[z_t^2]=1\).

a) i) Derive the expected value \(\mathbb{E}[S_T]\) using the linearity of the expectation operator. [2 marks]
ii) By expanding the expectation of the squared sum, derive the variance \(\text{Var}(S_T)\), clearly showing why the cross-terms vanish. [3 marks]

Asset prices are often modeled using a generalized random walk for daily log returns, given by \(r_t = \mu + \sigma z_t\), where \(z_t \sim \text{IID}(0,1)\). The cumulative log return over \(T\) periods is \(X_T = \sum_{t=1}^T r_t\).

a) i) Derive the expected cumulative return \(\mathbb{E}[X_T]\). [2 marks]
ii) Derive the variance \(\text{Var}(X_T)\) and demonstrate that it scales linearly with the time horizon \(T\). [3 marks]

A time series process is defined recursively by \(X_t = z_t + \theta z_{t-2}\), where the innovations \(z_t\) are independent and normalized random variables (mean zero, variance one).

a) i) Derive the variance of the process, \(\text{Var}(X_t)\). [2 marks]
ii) Derive the lag-2 autocovariance, defined as \(\gamma_2 = \mathbb{E}[X_t X_{t-2}]\). [3 marks]

The AR(1) process is often used to model mean reversion and is expressed as \[ R_t - \mu = -\lambda(R_{t-1} - \mu) + \sigma z_t \] where \(|\lambda| < 1\) and \(z_t \sim \text{IID}(0,1)\). Assume the process is weakly stationary.

a) i) By applying the unconditional expectation operator to both sides of the equation, derive \(\mathbb{E}[R_t]\). [2 marks]
ii) Using the assumption of stationarity (\(\text{Var}(R_t) = \text{Var}(R_{t-1}) = \gamma_0\)), substitute the equation of motion into \(\text{Var}(R_t) = \mathbb{E}[(R_t - \mu)^2]\) to derive the unconditional variance \(\gamma_0\). [4 marks]

The variance ratio test evaluates whether a stock price follows a random walk by analyzing aggregated returns. Let the \(q\)-period return be \[ r_t^{(q)} = \sum_{i=1}^q r_{t-i+1} \]

a) i) If the 1-period returns \(r_t\) are uncorrelated with a constant variance \(\sigma^2\), derive the variance of the aggregated return, \(\text{Var}(r_t^{(q)})\). [2 marks]
ii) Using your result from part (i), formulate the theoretical variance ratio \(\text{VR}(q)\) and state the exact value it must equal under the null hypothesis of a random walk. [2 marks]
